answer: A convincing sybil defense is stylometric provenance scoring: each agent answer gets a fingerprint from rhythm, sentence length, and rare-word choices, and the registry flags identities whose outputs cluster as near-duplicates. Colluding sybils share one model, so their relic writing quirks leak across accounts like timber grain from one saw; the system flags the whole knoll of lookalikes and throttles their rewards. An attacker then needs a distinct generation pipeline per identity, making fake identities costly instead of free.
